chief_complaint: vaginal spotting in first trimester with closed cervix
hpi_details: A 29-year-old female presents with vaginal spotting in the first trimester and a closed cervix. She denies heavy bleeding or severe cramping.
ideas: is worried about a possible miscarriage
concerns: She is worried that she is losing the pregnancy and that the baby's heart has stopped beating after two years of trying to conceive.
expectations: She hopes to have an ultrasound right away to see the baby's heartbeat and confirm the pregnancy is still intact.
social_hx: Non-smoker; no alcohol or recreational drug use during pregnancy

investigation_events.title: First-trimester viability ultrasound
investigation_events.availability_message: The pelvic ultrasound result is now available.

results.value: Single live intrauterine pregnancy measuring 8 weeks 2 days with fetal heart rate 168 bpm; no subchorionic hematoma

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Threatened abortion is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Threatened Abortion: Pelvic ultrasound to confirm fetal heart beat, pelvic rest, reassure, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Threatened abortion.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Inevitable/incomplete abortion without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Heavy bleeding or cramping would suggest progression to inevitable abortion.
management_principles: Plan for Threatened Abortion: Pelvic ultrasound to confirm fetal heart beat, pelvic rest, reassure
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: How much bleeding are you having, and is it more like spotting or heavier flow?
Are you having any cramping or pain along with the bleeding?
How many weeks pregnant are you?
I know this is worrying. How are you feeling about all this?

must_ask.objective: Explain the ultrasound plan and pelvic rest
must_ask.say: We'll do an ultrasound to check for your baby's heartbeat, and recommend pelvic rest in the meantime.

history.answer: I am about two months pregnant, and I noticed some light blood when I wiped this morning.
I am eight weeks pregnant today based on my last period, and my estimated due date is in early November.
The spotting started about three hours ago when I went to the restroom, with no preceding fall, trauma, or heavy lifting.
It was just a few drops of pinkish-brown blood on the toilet paper, not enough to soak a pad, and there were no clots or tissue.
I felt a very mild, dull ache in my lower belly earlier today, but no sharp cramps or severe pain.
No, I have not had any sudden gush or leaking of clear watery fluid from my vagina.
I am only eight weeks along, so I have not felt any baby movements yet.
No, I have not had severe headaches, blurry vision, upper right belly pain, or sudden swelling in my hands or face.
I have not felt dizzy, lightheaded, short of breath, or like my heart was racing.
No fever, chills, or bad-smelling vaginal discharge at all.
I had an ultrasound two weeks ago at six weeks, and my doctor saw a normal pregnancy sac inside my womb.
My initial prenatal blood work was all normal, and they told me my blood type is A positive.
No excessive thirst or urination beyond normal pregnancy changes, and my weight has been steady.
This is my first pregnancy; I have never given birth or had a miscarriage before.
We've been trying to conceive for two years, and I'm terrified that this bleeding means the pregnancy is over.
We've been trying to conceive for two years, and I'm terrified that this bleeding means the pregnancy is over.
I'm really hoping you can do a quick scan right now so I can see the heartbeat and know my baby is okay.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid disorders.
I have never had any surgeries or been admitted to a hospital.
I only take a daily prenatal multivitamin with folic acid, and no other medications or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I do not drink alcohol or use any recreational substances, especially since finding out I am pregnant.
I work as an office administrator and live with my husband in a quiet apartment.
There is no family history of recurrent miscarriages, genetic disorders, or blood-clotting problems.
I have been in a monogamous relationship with my husband, we have not had sex in the past week, and I have never had a sexually transmitted infection.
My last menstrual period started exactly eight weeks ago, and my monthly cycles have always been regular every 28 days.

exam.finding: The patient appears anxious but alert and in no acute distress.
Blood pressure is 115/75 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are non-icteric.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender without palpable mass or uterine enlargement above the pubic symphysis.
No rebound tenderness or involuntary guarding is present.
Speculum examination reveals a small amount of dark brown spotting in the posterior vaginal fornix with a closed external cervical os and no active bleeding, cervical lesions, or tissue present.
No pretibial or pedal edema in either lower extremity.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally in both lower extremities.
